findings.title: Pre-existing: POST /sign_up 500s (ActiveModel::UnknownAttributeError) when referral or other permitted non-attribute keys are present
findings.description: `create` passes the entire `sign_up_params` (merged into `expanded_params`) to `build_resource`, which is Devise `resource_class.new_with_session(hash, session)` -> `User.new(hash)` mass assignment. The permit list (line 310) includes seven keys that are NOT User attributes: `name`, `beta_token`, `registration_stripe_plan`, `referral`, `partner`, `organization_slug`, `login_intent` (verified: no users column, no attr_accessor in user.rb line 11 or any included concern — Settingsable/Friendlyable/CreatedViaAble define none, ApplicationRecord has no override, no method_missing). Mass-assigning any of them raises ActiveModel::UnknownAttributeError, and ApplicationController rescues only Pundit::NotAuthorizedError — raw 500. This is LIVE for `referral`: SignupForm.tsx line 25/66 sends `referral` in the register payload whenever `/register?referral=...` is in the URL (payload field and permit entry both pre-date this feature — confirmed via git diff 62dd55867..fc3f047f9 on useSession.ts, the old signature already had `referral`). So a password-path signup arriving with a referral tag gets a 500 and no account; Cypress registration.cy.js never catches it because it visits /register with no query params. `magic_create` is immune (its `user_params` is hand-built). Feature-relevant note: the four NEW params (`utm_source`, `utm_campaign`, `utm_data`, `internal_ref`) are real users columns (schema.rb users table), so this feature did NOT extend the crash surface — the new attribution keys are handled more safely than the pre-existing `referral`/`partner` analogs.
findings.recommendation: Report only (pre-existing, untouched semantics). Eventual fix belongs to its own scoped change: either drop the non-attribute keys from what reaches build_resource (e.g. `expanded_params.except(:referral, :partner, :name, :beta_token, :registration_stripe_plan, :organization_slug, :login_intent)`) or stop permitting keys `create` never consumes.

findings.title: Pre-existing: add_connect_user calls undefined `current_user` — NoMethodError 500 on returning-connect-user magic_create
findings.description: `add_connect_user` runs `current_user.update(current_connect_user: @connect_user)` when a ConnectUser record already exists. This controller inherits Devise::RegistrationsController (parent ApplicationController), not Api::V1::BaseController — the `alias current_user current_api_v1_user` lives only in Api::V1::BaseController line 9 and Connect::BaseController line 7, outside this ancestry, and ApplicationController defines no `current_user`. Devise defines only per-mapping helpers (`current_api_v1_user`, `current_admin_user`, `current_individual`, `current_api_public_v1_hire_user`); there is no bare `:user` mapping (devise_for :users is namespaced under api/v1 — routes.rb line 123). So `current_user` raises NameError/NoMethodError. Trigger path: magic_create with login_intent 'connect', an organization resolved from organization_slug, an existing CONFIRMED user, and an existing ConnectUser for that user+organization (line 121 -> line 249 find_by hit -> line 252). Even if a `current_user` helper existed it would be nil on this unauthenticated request — crash either way. Distinct from settled M2: M2 is the `organization.id`-on-nil crash inside the user_params connect branch (lines 88-101, new-user path, organization ABSENT); this is a different method (add_connect_user), a different nil (`current_user`), and the opposite precondition (organization PRESENT, returning user). Untouched by the feature diff — pre-existing.
findings.recommendation: Report only (pre-existing). A future scoped fix would update the found ConnectUser's owning user (`user.update(current_connect_user: @connect_user)`) or guard the line; needs Jessica's ruling on intended semantics since `user` (not a session user) is the record being logged in.

findings.title: Pre-existing: credential material printed to stdout in all environments (magic link record, generated password)
findings.description: Unconditional debug output (not gated on Rails.env.development?): `ap magic_link` (line 132) prints the MagicLink record — including its token/URL, a working login credential — on every existing-confirmed-user magic_create, in production too (the response itself withholds magic_url in production, line 143, so the log print defeats that gate at the infrastructure-log layer). `puts user_params` (line 164) prints the full new-user params hash including the `Devise.friendly_token(30)` password on every new-user magic_create. `puts params` (line 222) dumps raw params in magic_link_status. All three lines pre-date the feature (diff 62dd55867..fc3f047f9 does not touch them). Marginal feature interaction: user_params now also carries utm_source/utm_campaign/utm_data/internal_ref, so attribution values join the stdout dump — not sensitive, noted for completeness. This is adjacent to the baselined 'pre-existing ap debug lines in from_omniauth' but is a different file and a different consequence (credentials in logs, not debug noise), so reported separately as pre-existing.
findings.recommendation: Report only (pre-existing). Eventual cleanup: gate on Rails.env.development? like the neighboring Rails.logger.info lines, and never print user_params (contains password) or magic_link (contains token).

findings.title: Pre-existing: non-string `partner`/`referral` params crash `&.downcase` (type-confusion 500 for direct callers)
findings.description: `params[:partner]&.downcase` (lines 15, 91, 105) and `get_created_via`'s `partner_source&.downcase&.to_sym` / `referral_source&.downcase&.to_sym` (lines 343-344) read RAW params, not the permitted scalars — a crafted request sending `partner[]=x` or `partner[a]=b` yields an Array/Hash, and `&.downcase` raises NoMethodError (500). The live frontend always sends strings; direct-caller only. Pre-existing pattern, untouched by the feature; the new utm params are immune by construction (read through `sign_up_params`, whose scalar permits drop non-scalar values to nil, and utm_data is stored raw with no method calls on it).
findings.recommendation: Report only (pre-existing nitpick). A scoped hardening would read these through sign_up_params so non-scalars become nil.

notes: Read registrations_controller.rb in full at fc3f047f9 (attribution-work-qa), then isolated the feature delta with git diff 62dd55867..fc3f047f9: (a) sign_up_params gains :utm_source, :utm_campaign, :internal_ref and trailing utm_data: {} (line 310); (b) magic_create merges the four sign_up_params values into user_params in BOTH branches of the connect/default conditional (lines 97-100 and 110-113). Flows walked: new-user magic_create (recaptcha guard -> login_intent default -> org lookup -> both user_params branches -> find_by(email) nil -> build_resource/save -> columns assigned at creation; utm keys present in both branches, no key collisions with the base hash or merge, no guard between entry and the merge rejects utm-bearing requests); existing-confirmed branch and existing-unconfirmed branch (utm keys inert — only user_params[:email] is read; existing users' columns untouched, matching spec constraint 5); password create (expanded_params = sign_up_params.merge -> build_resource; the four flow as real column mass-assignments — users and organizations tables both verified in schema.rb to have the nullable no-default columns); connect-intent branch (M2 settled, not re-reported — but its neighbor add_connect_user yielded the distinct F2). Persistence mechanics verified against installed gems: utm_data arrives as permitted ActionController::Parameters; on the create path sanitize_for_mass_assignment deep-converts via to_h; on the magic_create path the Parameters object rides inside a plain Hash uncoverted, and jsonb serialization still works because actionpack 6.1.7.7 delegates as_json to @parameters (strong_parameters.rb line 246-247, read in the gem source) and ActiveSupport::JSON.encode uses as_json — no defect. Edge inputs checked: utm_data sent as scalar/array -> dropped by the hash permit -> nil column, no crash; utm_data sent as {} -> stored {} (raw-as-sent per D3, frontend never sends it); scalar utm params sent as arrays -> dropped to nil by scalar permit; empty-string utm_source stored raw per D3; absent params -> nil columns (no fallback fabrication anywhere in the new code). Analog structural matching: permit style matches the questions_controller.rb line 50 `options: {}` trailing-hash analog exactly; merge style mirrors the created_via/partner_source placement in both magic_create branches; guard ordering unchanged (recaptcha precedes all param handling, same as for the referral/partner analogs); neighboring omniauth_callbacks_controller reads the same four keys from merged_tracking string-keys into the from_omniauth keyword call, creation-time-only on both paths — consistent. Deliberate spec-mandated differences from the analogs confirmed as such (raw storage/no downcase vs partner_source's &.downcase; org copy deferred to organizations#create per D5 instead of the partner org-update-at-registration pattern at line 43-45/182-184). Rescue coverage checked: only Pundit::NotAuthorizedError is rescued, so F1/F2 surface as raw 500s. Not reported per settled rulings/baselines: M2 connect-branch organization.id nil crash; uncapped server-side sizes (M1); bracket-key 400s (M3). Judged not findings: sign_up_params invoked ~8x per magic_create request (re-runs permit; trivial); user-enumeration surface of magic_link_status/magic_create response variants (pre-existing design, recaptcha-tempered); find_by-then-create email race (pre-existing, unique index on email turns it into a 500 not a duplicate). No feature-introduced defect found in this file: zero BLOCKER/HIGH; 3 MED + 1 LOW, all pre-existing.
